why_suggested: This is the rotation assumed to be in use now. It is the baseline the others are compared with.

rotations.label: Groundnut one year, millet the next

why_suggested: Its crops need less water over the year.
evidence: Groundnut: rain and stored soil water met 71% of crop water need in a typical year and 61% in a poor year (1 in 4); 5 of 45 seasons fell below 50%.
Millet: rain and stored soil water met 76% of crop water need in a typical year and 64% in a poor year (1 in 4); 4 of 45 seasons fell below 50%.
benefits: Alternating crop families interrupts pests and diseases that build up under one crop.
Crop water need averages 441 mm a year against 511 mm for the current rotation (14% less).
information_gaps: Soil water-holding capacity is assumed (100 mm), not measured for this location.

rotations.label: Millet, then chickpea on late rains

why_suggested: It keeps the field covered for more of the year.
evidence: Millet: rain and stored soil water met 67% of crop water need in a typical year and 56% in a poor year (1 in 4); 9 of 45 seasons fell below 50%.
Chickpea (Bengal gram): rain and stored soil water met 53% of crop water need in a typical year and 43% in a poor year (1 in 4); 20 of 44 seasons fell below 50%.
benefits: About 2.6 fewer bare months a year, which reduces exposure of the soil to erosion.
Alternating crop families interrupts pests and diseases that build up under one crop.
information_gaps: This result depends strongly on how much water the soil holds: the weakest crop gets 46% of its water need with 75 mm of soil storage and 69% with 200 mm. Local soil data is needed before relying on it.
Chickpea (Bengal gram): season length is a placeholder, not from a published table.
